parsed_answer.content:
SonarQube is an enterprise-grade static analysis platform designed to manage technical debt by inspecting source code for bugs, vulnerabilities, and code smells. It acts as a continuous inspection tool that integrates into your CI/CD pipeline, providing a centralized dashboard to track the health of your codebase over time. Unlike a simple linter, SonarQube maintains a historical state, allowing teams to enforce 'Quality Gates'—thresholds that, if failed, prevent a build from being promoted to production. It operates by parsing your source code into an Abstract Syntax Tree (AST) and running a suite of rules against it to identify deviations from best practices, security flaws, and maintainability issues.

Code coverage is a quantitative metric that measures the percentage of your source code executed by automated tests. It is a proxy for confidence, ensuring that your unit tests touch the lines of logic you have written. However, high coverage does not imply high quality; you can have 100% coverage with poorly written, unmaintainable, or logically flawed code. Conversely, code quality is a qualitative assessment of the codebase's structural integrity. It encompasses cyclomatic complexity, adherence to design patterns, naming conventions, and the absence of 'code smells'—patterns that indicate deeper design problems. While coverage tells you if you are testing your code, quality tells you if your code is worth testing in the first place.

items: SonarQube uses the SonarScanner to analyze the project, which then sends the report to the SonarQube Server. The server performs deep analysis on the AST to identify complex issues like SQL injection or resource leaks.
Quality Gates are the enforcement mechanism. They define conditions like 'No new critical vulnerabilities' or 'Maintainability rating of A', which are evaluated after every analysis.

Code coverage is typically calculated by instrumentation tools like JaCoCo in the Java ecosystem. JaCoCo modifies the bytecode during execution to track which branches and lines are visited, feeding this data back to SonarQube.
Technical debt in SonarQube is calculated by estimating the time required to fix all identified issues, providing a concrete business value to the 'cost' of ignoring code quality.

parsed_answer.content: Senior Insight: Do not fall into the 'Coverage Trap.' Chasing 100% coverage often leads to 'test-induced damage,' where developers write brittle tests that assert on implementation details rather than behavior. Always prioritize Quality Gates that focus on 'New Code' rather than the entire legacy codebase; cleaning up existing technical debt is a marathon, but preventing new debt is a mandatory daily requirement.

title: What is SonarQube? Code coverage vs Code quality?
